about: The Magníficat is Mary’s canticle from the Gospel according to Saint Luke (Luke 1:46–55), sung at Roman Vespers. This edition preserves the traditional Latin text and its ten numbered biblical verses, followed separately by the Glory Be doxology.

seg.tr: And my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.
For He has regarded the lowliness of His handmaid: behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed.

ex.w015: Greek ταπείνωσις confirms that Mary speaks of her low estate, not in praise of a moral achievement of her own.
ex.w026: “Generations”, not “nations”: all the ages to come will call her blessed.

seg.tr: For He who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is His name.
And His mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear Him.

ex.w045: The word names those who fear God and toward whom His mercy extends.

seg.tr: He has shown might with His arm; He has scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart.

ex.w048: “Fecit poténtiam” means literally that He wrought or showed strength.
ex.w056: The pronoun refers to the proud: it is the designs of their hearts that are scattered.

seg.tr: He has put down the mighty from their seat, and has exalted the humble.
He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
He has received Israel His servant, being mindful of His mercy.

ex.w071: The verb presents God coming to the aid of Israel, His servant.
ex.w073: Greek παῖς confirms that Israel is called God’s servant here, not a boy.

seg.tr: As He spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever.

ex.w080: With “locútus” it forms the single predicate “has spoken”.

seg.tr: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

ex.w090: Latin leaves “sit” unspoken: “Glória [sit] Patri” — “glory [be] to the Father”.

seg.tr: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
